dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Kevin.
Yes, hello. Good morning. I am calling about a sidewalk. I know it is Saturday and City Hall is closed, so I called the storm line number, the one on the recording. I hope this is the right one.
Yeah, you're in the right place. We pick up here on weekends for snow stuff. What's going on with the sidewalk?

It is the sidewalk by the school. Near the corner, on the side where the children walk in. It was never cleared. Not shoveled, not plowed, nothing. We had the dusting Thursday night, and it is so cold now that everything froze. It is ice, with the footprints frozen in it.
Okay, yeah, that cold snap's not helping. A dusting turns into a skating rink real quick. Which school are we talking about?
The one near my house. I am at 192 Kay Street. The school is down the block, maybe two minutes walking. The sidewalk I mean is on the school side, from the corner to the crosswalk.
Got it, 192 Kay Street, Historic Hill. So the stretch from the corner down to the crosswalk, school side. Let me write that down. Never cleared at all?

Never. I walked it this morning to check. The other side has a path, someone did it, a little. But this side, no. And I am not complaining about the dusting, you understand. A dusting is nothing. It is that nobody came after. This happens every time. Every time it is the same sidewalk.
Okay. When you say every time, you've seen it happen with other storms this winter?
Yes. In December also, the bigger snow. I waited three days then. I did not call then, I thought, they will come. They did not come. So now I call.
Fair enough. I'm noting it down as a repeat. Can I ask, is there a reason you're out there today? Just so I have it for the notes.

Yes. I am chaperoning a class trip. To a farm, with the second grade. We meet at the school at one o'clock, the bus leaves from there. Twenty-two children, and the parents, and some of them are small, you know. If one falls on this ice, on the way to the bus, it is a problem. So I want it cleared before one.

Oh, okay, that changes the timing. Honestly, I can't promise a crew gets there in the next hour and a half. But I'll log it as a school-access sidewalk and mark it urgent, and I'll pass it to whoever's dispatching today.
Please log it, yes. I want it on the record that I called today, Saturday, in the morning, and that it was reported. Because if it is not written down, then next week they say nobody told us.

Totally. It's logged with the date and time. Saturday, eleven-thirty or so. Let me read it back. Sidewalk on the school side near Kay Street, corner to crosswalk, never cleared after Thursday night's snow, icy, repeat issue from December, caller chaperoning a school trip at one. That sound right?
Almost. The snow was Thursday night, yes, but I think it was early Friday morning that it ended. Thursday night into Friday. But Thursday night is fine, that is close.
Thursday night into Friday morning, I'll put that. Thanks for the correction.
And one more detail. The school has a gate, a side gate, and the ice is worst right in front of it. By the gate. Where the water comes off the roof and freezes.
Right in front of the side gate, worst spot. Got it. Is that the gate the kids use for the buses, or a different one?
The same one. The bus waits there. So everybody walks across it.
Okay, that's useful. I'll flag it. Do you want a call back when it's been looked at? I've got a number here, but I'd rather confirm it.
Yes. It is four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-six-seven. This is my cell. The signal is okay here.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-six-seven. Perfect. And it's Mr. Figueroa, right? F-I-G-U-E-R-O-A?
Yes, Luis Figueroa. That is correct.

Great. So, Luis, here's what I'd do in the meantime. If you've got any salt or sand, even a bucket, a little on that spot by the gate would help before the kids come. I know that's not your job, and I'm not asking you to. Just a practical thing.

I have some salt in the garage. I can bring it. But it is the city's sidewalk, and I am seventy-something years old, carrying a bucket. I will do it today for the children. But I want it noted that it should not be me.
Understood, and I'll put that in too. You shouldn't have to. Someone will get a look at this, I just can't tell you the hour.
Okay. I understand you are one person on the telephone. I am not angry with you. I am only tired of calling about the same sidewalk.
No, that's fair, and I appreciate you saying it. It's on the sheet now with the December history, so it won't look like a first-time thing.
Good. Then I will go and put the salt. Thank you, Kevin.
Thanks for calling, Luis. Enjoy the farm, and watch your footing out there.
Yes, yes. Goodbye.
